newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse trade up with futures.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse trade up with futures.

text.p: German shares, shrugging off the directionless mood of the last few days, took a turn upwards at Friday's bourse open as the knock-on effect of the expiry of DAX futures exerted a positive influence.

The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares rose 17.06 points or 0.65 percent to 2,641.50, but dealers remarked that turnover was small and likely to remain so before the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to consider U.S. interest rates next week.
"From the client side, trade is pretty thin. It looks as if most of it is coming from the derivatives side, one said.
The December DAX future contract traded 15.5 points up at 2,659.5 after the expiry of the September contract.
Stronger German Bunds and the firmer dollar were also seen as supporting shares before the September 24 meeting of the Federal Reserve.

Electronics group Siemens AG, up 51 pfennigs at 79.23 marks, was seen as benefitting from the stronger U.S. currency and the firm performance of U.S. high-tech stocks on Wall Street Thursday night amid a mixed overall market.
Export-led stocks such as Bayer AG, Hoechst AG and BASF AG in the chemicals sector all gained on the dollar's strength, as did vehicle-maker Daimler-Benz AG, up 80 pfennnigs at 83.95.

Traders said Daimler also benefitted from positive comments coming from the Hannover truck fair, where its Mercedes-Benz unit indicated it was confident of record sales in its commercial vehicle side.
